text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The rector of Vilnius University said he will carry out a policy of positive discrimination in favour of women.

- Lithuania and Poland believe that the NATO expansion process will be started at the Madrid Summit and will be open for all candidate countries, a declaration signed by the two presidents, Algirdas Brazauskas and Aleksander Kwasniewski said.
- An Austrian embassy was opened in Vilnius on Thursday.
- Parliament passed a law aimed at fighting money laundering. Finance institions are obliged to identify and inform about bank transactions exceeding 50 million litas.
- Lithuanian Gas firm posted a 35.2 million litas pre-tax profit in the first five months of the year.
- The temporary administrator of liquidated Innovation Bank may be offered the post of chairman of the board of the state-run Savings Bank at the bank's council meeting on Friday.
- Lithuanian and Russian delegations continued negotiations over the delimitation of the state border between the two countries.
- Negotiations over the disputed territory in the Baltic sea between Lithuania and Latvia will be held in Vilnius on July 26.
- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta has offered to reduce fines to 10 percent from 25 percent of annual turnover for companies which evade tax.
- House of Prince Lietuva was fined 22,494 litas for violating lottery rules during an advertising campaign.
- Individuals' deposits in state-run Savings Bank topped one billion litas. The bank has 57 percent of the market.
